title: Prepare a Fresh Citrus Salad with Thin Orange Slices
meta_description: Elevate your greens with this refreshing citrus salad. Learn how to create the perfect mandoline orange slices salad for restaurant-quality results at home.
html:
There is nothing quite like the burst of sunshine that fresh citrus brings to a winter table. While we often think of oranges as a snack for peeling on the go, slicing them thin transforms them into a sophisticated culinary ingredient. If you want to take your greens to the next level, learning to make a mandoline orange slices salad is a game-changer for both texture and presentation.

Why Thin Slices Make All the Difference

When you chop an orange into chunks, the fruit tends to be mushy and releases juice rapidly, drowning the greens in a pool of liquid. By slicing the citrus crosswise into thin rounds, you maintain the structural integrity of the fruit segments. This method creates beautiful, translucent wheels that allow the dressing to coat the surface without turning the entire bowl into a soup.

Getting that consistent, paper-thin cut by hand can be difficult and dangerous. A sharp knife requires a steady hand and significant knife skills to get the slices even. This is where a high-quality tool comes in handy. Your standard chef’s knife can do the job, but to get that restaurant-quality presentation, I reach for my Mandoline Slicer. Restaurant-thin, even slices of veggies and fruit fast — adjustable mandolines with hand guards make the process incredibly efficient and safe.

Selecting the Best Citrus

The flavor of your dish depends entirely on the produce you pick. Since the citrus is the star of the show, avoid fruit that feels light for its size or has soft spots. You want fruit that feels heavy and dense, indicating it is full of juice.

For a visually stunning salad, mix varieties. Navel oranges are sweet and classic, but adding blood oranges provides a deep ruby color and a tart, berry-like finish. A pink grapefruit or a Meyer lemon can add a necessary acidic note to cut through the sweetness. Don't be afraid to slice up a lime if you want a real zing, though peel them first as lime rind can be tough.

Choosing Citrus for Your Mandoline Orange Slices Salad

Preparation is key before you even turn on the blade. You have a choice regarding the peel. Leaving the skin on adds a bitter contrast and a vibrant pop of color, but you must ensure the slices are razor-thin so the peel isn't chewy. If you prefer a sweeter, more delicate bite, take the time to cut the top and bottom off the orange and slice the peel and pith away with a knife before using the mandoline.

When you are ready to slice, set your Mandoline Slicer to the thinnest setting, usually around 1/8th of an inch or thinner. Secure the fruit firmly with the hand guard. Slide the orange down the blade in smooth, confident motions. The adjustable settings on the mandoline allow you to switch instantly between thick heirloom tomatoes for a burger and these delicate orange slices for a salad.

Assembling the Mandoline Orange Slices Salad

Once your citrus is prepped, the assembly is quick. The base of the salad should be something sturdy but slightly bitter to stand up to the sweet fruit. Arugula, radicchio, or baby kale are excellent choices.

Here is a simple method for building the bowl:

  1. Wash and dry your greens thoroughly. Wet greens will dilute the vinaigrette.
  2. Spread the greens across a large platter or shallow bowl.
  3. Arrange the citrus wheels on top of the greens. Fan them out slightly so they don't overlap too much, showcasing the symmetry achieved by your Mandoline Slicer.
  4. Add texture. Thinly sliced red onion or radish adds a nice crunch and a spicy bite.
  5. Finish with cream. Add crumbled feta, goat cheese, or dollops of burrata to provide a rich, savory element.

The Dressing: A Sweet-Tart Balance

Because the oranges are so juicy, you don't need a heavy, cream-based dressing. A simple vinaigrette is best. I like to whisk together extra virgin olive oil, a splash of champagne vinegar (or apple cider vinegar), a teaspoon of Dijon mustard, and a teaspoon of honey. The honey helps emulsify the oil and vinegar while amplifying the natural sugars in the mandoline orange slices salad.

Fresh herbs are non-negotiable here. Mint is the classic pairing for citrus, offering a cool, refreshing contrast to the sweet acidity. Alternatively, thinly sliced basil or fresh dill can work beautifully depending on your cheese choice. Toss the greens with just enough dressing to coat, then drizzle a little extra oil over the citrus slices themselves to make them glisten.

FAQ

Do I have to peel the oranges before slicing them on the mandoline?

Not necessarily. If you leave the peel on, make sure your Mandoline Slicer is set to a very thin setting so the rind is palatable and not tough. If you prefer a sweeter salad, peel the oranges completely so you are only slicing the fruit segments and juice.

How do I store leftover sliced salad?

Citrus salads are best eaten immediately. The acid in the oranges and the dressing will wilt greens like arugula very quickly. If you must store it, keep the dressing separate and store the sliced oranges and greens in an airtight container in the fridge for up to one day, though the texture will suffer.

Can I use this technique for other fruits?

Absolutely. The Mandoline Slicer is perfect for creating thin, even slices of other firm fruits like apples, pears, kiwis, and even strawberries. Just ensure the fruit is firm enough to hold its shape against the blade.
